maria: heads-up — after the 2026-03 runtime deploy we saw a 25-40% p95 latency spike on Qwen2.5 for our mixed Latin/CJK workload :thinking:
maria: repro steps: batch of 8, seq_len ~64 but ~30% of inputs contain CJK chars.
maria: profiler shows kernel selection flipping between fast_fused_attn and fallback_mm for certain batches. payload: tokenized lengths look fine, but kv cache hit ratio drops for those mixed batches. logs:```
[2026-03-17T14:02:11Z] kernel_autotuner: selected=fast_fused_attn, score=12.4
[2026-03-17T14:02:11Z] kernel_autotuner: selected=fallback_mm, score=12.3
[2026-03-17T14:02:11Z] kvcache: hits=0.62, misses=0.38
[2026-03-17T14:02:11Z] latency_ms p95=124  (baseline 88)
```
maria: attaching minimal repro gist (token lists + raw bytes) — https://intra.gist/qwen2p5-cjk-batch-repro
kevin: interesting — autotuner oscillation suggests score differences are small and maybe non-deterministic perf noise. but why kvcache hit ratio drops?
ash: (typo -> ash) I dug into tokenizer alignment: for CJK we sometimes emit single-char tokens that change RoPE position mapping for the whole sequence when mixed with latin multi-byte tokens. that changes kv positions and breaks prefix reuse across batches with similar content.
ash: quick diagram: if tokenization compresses latin words to fewer tokens, the positional indices shift, so cached KV entries don't line up when we try to reuse across requests in the same batch slot.
ora: that matches a case I saw with zh+en pair tests — cache keys include absolute position index, so any tokenization variation shifts future cache lookups.
kevin: ah — so it's not cache eviction but key mismatch. can we normalize tokenization (e.g., NFKC) before tokenizing to reduce variance?
ash: norm helps some, but the root is token boundary variance across languages. also RoPE scaling heuristic we use multiplies pos indices by 1.0 for latin-heavy and 0.98 for CJK-heavy to match upstream model configs; that scaling introduces tiny positional drifts that make caches incompatible between policy variants.
maria: so two potential failure modes: kernel_autotuner jitter + kvcache key mismatch due to pos scaling/ tokenization differences.
kevin: reproduce plan: 1) run microbench that pins kernel selection deterministically (force fast_fused_attn) 2) run with and w/o tokenizer normalization 3) toggle RoPE scaling flag per batch and measure kv hit ratio.
kevin: can someone produce the microbench? I can patch autotuner to expose a debug flag.
nash: I have a small harness already: `eng/runtime/tools/kernbench.py --model qwen2.5 --batch 8 --mix-cjk 0.3 --seed 42 --force-kernel fast_fused_attn`
nash: sample results I ran locally:
```
--force fast_fused_attn, norm on: kv_hit=0.89, p95=92ms
--force fast_fused_attn, norm off: kv_hit=0.64, p95=126ms
--autotune, norm on: kv_hit=0.81, p95=100ms (autotuner chose fused 83% samples)
--autotune, norm off: kv_hit=0.60, p95=130ms (autotuner flipped kernels a lot)
```
nora: those numbers strongly point to tokenization variance being the main driver. autotuner amplifies it by changing kernels mid-flight.
kevin: two mitigations: (A) make kvcache keys robust to small pos-scale differences (eg. quantize positions before keying), (B) prefer kernel stickiness for a small window for same batch signature so autotuner doesn't flip for tiny score deltas.
maria: both sound reasonable. quick note: quantizing positions might slightly affect model perf if we change pos indexes, needs eval.
ash: quantize to nearest 0.25 multiplier; shouldn't change attention patterns materially. we can run unit eval on heldout prompts.
ora: also consider normalizing tokenization outputs for multi-lang requests in the edge router: add a pretokenize normalization step for messages flagged as multi-script. cheap and may avoid kv drift entirely.
kevin: roadmap: 1) perf patch: sticky_autotune with window=10s AND threshold delta=1.5% to avoid flips. 2) kvkey: quantize pos to 0.25 increments. 3) router: opt-in normalization flag for multi-script workloads.
ora: I'll open PRs: router-normalize and kvkey-quantize. maria — can you create a canary run config?
maria: yes — will create a dedicated canary pool and route 2% of traffic for 24h to validate. will include perf and correctness evals.
perf-bot: [metric alert] qwen2.5_p95_latency increased by 32% in region-us-west-2 at 2026-03-17T14:06:00Z
kevin: thanks perf-bot. once PRs are up let's run microbench and then test canary. keep the autotuner patch gated behind a runtime flag.
maria: quick note for release notes: mention "mixed-script tokenization impacting kv cache & autotuner oscillation" — will draft.
nash: small hack: for immediate mitigation we can add router-side header `x-rt-tokenize:norm` for customers opt-in. low-risk.
maria: ok I'll enable it for the affected customer and monitor.
kevin: can we also add a unit test that fuzzes mixed language tokenizations and validates kvcache key stability?
nora: yes — I'll add to eng-runtime tests: `tests/tokenization/mixed_script_kv_stability.py` with randomized seeds.
maria: thanks all. follow-ups: PR links when ready, I'll schedule canary next 24h window. :thumbsup:
